summary: This article explains what an archipelago is, how islands form through volcanoes, hotspots, and coral, and why island-chain nations like Indonesia and the Philippines are geographically unique.
introduce: Read the title “Archipelagos: Chains of Islands” aloud and ask each student to write one question they hope the article will answer. Collect a few questions, then explain that today they will find the one big idea that ties all the details together.

keyTerms.def: a large group or chain of islands
formed by a volcano or by rising magma
a hard, rock-like material built by colonies of tiny sea animals

challengeTerms.def: the process in which one tectonic plate slowly sinks beneath another plate
found naturally in only one place in the world and nowhere else
the wide variety of living things found in a place

discussion: Do you agree or disagree that living spread across thousands of islands creates very different challenges than living on one connected piece of land? Use evidence from the article to explain.
Compare how a volcanic island forms with how a coral island forms.
struggling: Pre-teach archipelago, volcanic, and coral with pictures or gestures, then let weak readers complete a main-idea-and-details web with a partner.
gifted: Ask strong readers to read a challenging version and write a short paragraph that uses subduction, endemic, and biodiversity to state the main idea of the article in their own words.
